content.comment_body: Hello, My installation of [product_name] [version_no] suddenly stopped working. I faced this issue previously and managed to fix it, but the problem has returned. Unfortunately, the original installation media is lost due to multiple moves. Older software versions still run fine, but since converting files to the latest hardware version, I can't access them with older applications. When launching the newest version, the splash screen appears briefly before closing. I've attached a video demonstrating the issue. I appreciate anyone's help, as I'm preparing for major projects and need to continue programming. For reference: Windows 11 Pro 64bit, version 22H2, 4GB RAM. Kind regards, [user_name]
If you've also installed an older version of [product_name] on your PC, try upgrading to [version_no]. You can find the upgrade at: [url]
I tried that solution, but unfortunately, it didn't resolve the issue. The splash screen still flashes briefly before the software closes.
Did you first uninstall the problematic version, restart your computer, and then reinstall the software? Make sure to run the installer as administrator.

I followed those steps as well, but I encountered the same results. I also ran both the installer and executable in compatibility mode, but it didn't help. Can [product_name] [version_no] actually operate on Windows 11, or do I need to revert to an earlier Windows version?
The manual states compatibility with Windows 7, Windows 8, and Windows 10. Refer to the attached documentation. If I were you, I'd submit a support request.
Hello [user_name], I'm experiencing the same issue. Was it resolved? If so, could you share how you fixed it? Best regards

Hello [user_name], Based on what you've described, Windows 11 often causes significant issues with older software. After Windows 7, I switched to a BSD/Linux OS and now use a virtual machine running Windows 7 to use [product_name]. Consider setting up a VM with Windows 7 in Virtual Box and install only the required software. This approach could help and allows for easier migration to another computer. Regards, [user_name]
Thank you [user_name], My technical knowledge is quite limited, but maybe I can find someone to help me with your suggestion. Regards, [user_name]

Dear all, It's frustrating that no one from [company_name] responds. I have the exact same problem on two machines (laptop and desktop), both running Windows 11 64-bit. [version_no] works fine, but [version_no] and later won't start at all. Has anyone from [company_name] responded? The support is disappointing—I've sent multiple emails with no reply.

From [company_name], I had to reinstall Java since it was missing from my laptop. See attached documentation. After reinstalling Windows 11 Pro and [product_name] [version_no], it worked again. The issue seems related to importing UDFs from an earlier software version into [version_no], which causes problems. I reinstalled Windows 11 Pro and now avoid using UDFs in this version. Regards, [user_name]
I've found an easier solution: If you save the UDF files in a new folder on your laptop, [product_name] [version_no] works again. Regards, [user_name]
That solution worked! Thank you very much.
I'm experiencing the same issue. Is there any solution available?
Could you clarify what 'the same problem' is?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing issues where [product_name] [version_no] and subsequent versions fail to start on Windows 11, only displaying a brief splash screen before closing unexpectedly. Earlier versions of the software operate properly, but converted projects aren't compatible with them, leading to workflow disruptions. Users are frustrated by the lack of official support and delayed responses from [company_name], which impedes their programming and project progress.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] [version_no] to function reliably on Windows 11 and hope for timely support and responses from [company_name] regarding compatibility issues.
